sourcePolicy: All questions in this pack are Ready2Go original draft practice items unless an individual record states otherwise. No official JAMB past-question corpus is included. Human subject-matter and answer-key review is required before public release.

questions.question: Pitch describes how high or low a sound is perceived to be. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Pitch relates to perceived highness or lowness of sound.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: The organisation of sounds and silences in time is called what?
questions.explanation: Rhythm organises durations and accents in time.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A sequence of notes perceived as a musical line is called what?
questions.explanation: Melody is a succession of pitches forming a musical line.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Tempo indicates what?
questions.explanation: Tempo is the pace of music.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Dynamics in music refer to changes in what?
questions.explanation: Dynamics indicate relative sound intensity.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: The five horizontal lines used in standard Western notation form what?
questions.explanation: Musical notes are placed on a staff.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Which clef is commonly used for higher-pitched parts?
questions.explanation: Treble clef commonly notates higher pitches.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Harmony generally involves what?

options.A: Notes sounding together in chords or related combinations
options.B: Only one note at a time

questions.explanation: Harmony concerns simultaneous pitches and their relationships.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Timbre helps distinguish instruments even when they play the same pitch and loudness. It refers to what?
questions.explanation: Timbre is the quality that differentiates sound sources.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A symbol indicating silence for a specific duration is called what?
questions.explanation: A rest represents a period of silence.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Which family includes violin, viola and cello?
questions.explanation: The violin family consists of bowed string instruments.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: The grouping of beats into recurring patterns is called what?
questions.explanation: Metre organises beats into recurring strong and weak patterns.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A conductor primarily helps an ensemble coordinate what?
questions.explanation: Conductors coordinate timing and ensemble interpretation.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A talking drum can vary its sound partly by changing what?

options.B: The length of a football field

questions.explanation: Pressure on the drumhead alters pitch, enabling speech-like patterns.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A composer is a person who primarily does what?
questions.explanation: Composers write or create musical works.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.
